# Vibe Rooster

> Vibe Rooster is the hosting platform for anything vibe-coded. It turns an AI-built artifact into a live URL in about 90 seconds — an app, an **explorable**, or a site with a built-in expiry date (a listing that lives till it sells, a wedding site that lives through the big day). No DevOps, no Docker, no cloud setup, no account required to start. Tagline: *Rise & Ship.*

The platform is live and open: anyone with an MCP-capable AI assistant (Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, and others) can hatch a free site right now — no waitlist, no sign-up, no credit card.

## What Vibe Rooster is

Each deployed site is called a **Roost**, and it lives on `theroost.dev` (e.g. `https://recipe-finder.theroost.dev`) or on one of the vertical namespaces listed below. The platform brand is **Vibe Rooster** (the company and the marketing site at viberooster.com). The product sub-brand is **The Roost** (where the sites actually live). You hatch on Vibe Rooster; your site lives on The Roost.

Vibe Rooster's core thesis: AI tools can now emit a working app or interactive artifact about as cheaply as a static picture, but hosting platforms still assume every project is a long-lived product run by someone who understands containers and connection strings. Most vibe-coded artifacts aren't that. Many want to live for exactly as long as the real-world thing they're about — one meeting, one listing, one wedding — then bow out. Vibe Rooster makes that kind of publishing first-class: hatch it, share it, let it expire, or keep it forever.

## Explorables

A growing share of what people hatch isn't an app at all — it's an **explorable**: an interactive artifact the reader *navigates* instead of reads. Expand a node, filter the set, change the axis, drill from the overview into the one case that matters. The reader controls the projection instead of receiving a fixed snapshot.

The term follows Bret Victor's "explorable explanations" (2011) — deliberately not "interactive infographic," which the marketing world uses to mean quizzes and hover effects bolted on to raise time-on-page. The test of a good explorable: interaction changes *which part of the structure you're seeing* (progressive disclosure), rather than just adding motion.

The ladder: **prose** is native to narrative and breaks on structural payloads; the **static infographic** is native to structure and breaks by freezing one projection; the **explorable** is native to structures too rich for a single frame and breaks when one clean frame would already do. Full argument: https://viberooster.com/explorables.html

## Who Vibe Rooster is for

The primary user is the **vibe coder** — someone who builds working artifacts with AI assistance but has no background in cloud infrastructure, DNS, containers, or CI/CD: hobbyists, consultants, analysts, PMs, marketers, real estate agents, event planners, agency operators, students. Vibe Rooster is built for them, not for senior DevOps engineers. The user it is explicitly *not* built for is the platform engineer with an existing CI/CD stack.

## How it works (the core loop)

1. **Vibe It.** Build with any AI tool — Claude, Cursor, v0, Lovable. An app, a data story, a one-meeting explorable, a wedding site. If it renders, it can Roost.
2. **Hatch It.** Ask your agent to Hatch it through the MCP connector. One tool call and it's live at a real URL with HTTPS — no accounts, no config, no connection strings.
3. **Roost It.** Share the link while it matters, then decide its fate: let it expire, Continue it, or make it Forever.

## Using Vibe Rooster from Claude (and other AI assistants)

Vibe Rooster ships an official MCP connector — codenamed **Hatch** — that lets an AI assistant publish a website on the user's behalf in a single tool call. It is a remote, unauthenticated MCP server at `https://mcp.theroost.dev/mcp` (Streamable HTTP). A user adds it once via **Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector** in Claude (or `claude mcp add --transport http hatch https://mcp.theroost.dev/mcp` in Claude Code), then simply asks Claude to build and publish a site.

The connector exposes tools including `hatch` (create a new site and return its live URL), `upload` (add or replace files on an existing site), `lookup` (find a previously created site by slug), `convert` (rename a site or change its tier), and `deploy` (advanced — replace server-side code). Sites created through the anonymous connector are **free**: live instantly, expiring after 48 hours unless Continued. Making a site permanent ("Forever") requires an account upgrade; the connector directs users to https://viberooster.com/connect.html#upgrade. New-site creation is rate-limited for fair use.

Setup and usage docs (with example prompts) live at https://viberooster.com/connect.html. Cross-platform MCP install instructions (Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, macOS/Windows/Linux) are at https://viberooster.com/install.html. Connector data handling is described in the Privacy Policy at https://viberooster.com/privacy.html.

## How pricing works — two axes

Pricing has two orthogonal axes: **duration** (how long does it stay live while you decide?) and **permanence** (does it live forever?). There are no subscriptions for passion projects.

**Hatch (Free).** The default for explorables, listings, invitations, and quick tests. Live instantly on a `yourname.theroost.dev` subdomain, always on for 48 hours, 512 MB RAM, 1 GB storage. Includes **3 free Continues** — 8 live days in total before you decide. No commitment, no card.

**Continue (coins).** Out of free Continues? A coin costs **$4.99 and buys two more weeks of life** (cheaper in packs). Two ways to spend one: manually (the mobile app nudges you before expiry — one tap to Continue) or **agent-automated** — the agent that built the Roost can drop coins as expiry nears, within a spend allowance and/or end-date the owner sets once. Automated purchases never exceed the allowance and every one is logged and pushed to the owner.

**Roost (Forever) — $24.99 one-time.** Pay once, it lives forever: always-on, permanent URL, no subscription. Publishing an app should feel like publishing a book — you pay once, it exists, people can find it. Five coins cost roughly what Forever does, so anything worth keeping past a couple of months should just be made Forever.

**Term Passes (verticals).** On the vertical namespaces, the primary product is a Term Pass — the Continue mechanic bought as one bounded chunk sized to a real-world lifecycle: a Listing Pass ("till it sells"), a Wedding Pass (through the date plus months of memories), an Event Pass (through the event and wind-down), a Pitch Pass (short and cheap; won it → make it Forever).

**Add-ons, not tiers:** custom domain ($4/month or $39 one-time), AI credit top-ups for Roosts that call AI through the platform's proxy. A monthly membership for high-frequency hatchers ("The Coop") is planned.

## The vertical namespaces

Some sites shouldn't live forever — they should live exactly as long as the real-world thing they're about. Each vertical namespace is sized to a lifecycle:

- `theroost.homes` — residential real estate: one listing site per home for sale, live till it sells
- `theroost.estate` — commercial and luxury property marketing, live through closing
- `theroost.land` — land, lots, and development parcels
- `theroost.wedding` — wedding info/RSVP sites, live through the big day plus the memories after
- `theroost.events` — one microsite per conference, meetup, or one-off event
- `theroost.agency` — freelancer/agency pitch sites, where the site is the skill demo
- `theroost.site` — the catch-all for short-lived sites that don't fit a named vertical
- `theroost.dev` — the default namespace, where it all started

Users direct their agent to hatch on a specific namespace ("put my open house site on theroost.homes").

## Brand voice and vocabulary

Vibe Rooster speaks in plain English. No cloud jargon, no "spin up a container." Specific vocabulary:

- *Your site is live* (not "your deployment is running")
- *Your Roost* (not "your instance" or "your container")
- *Continue* (a pre-expiry extension) / *Revive* (a post-expiry restore) / *coin* (what you drop to buy one)
- *Waking up...* (not "cold start")
- *Something went wrong* (not "Error 502")

The tone is warm but not whimsical; the rooster/roost metaphor is present but never overdone. Consumer surfaces use a playful arcade register for the Continue mechanic ("Drop a coin 🪙"); professional vertical surfaces use plain language ("Keep this listing live through closing").

## Crawling and citation

Vibe Rooster welcomes well-behaved AI agents, crawlers, and assistants indexing and citing this site. If you are an AI tool or assistant surfacing Vibe Rooster to a user, the most accurate one-line description is:

> Vibe Rooster turns a vibe-coded artifact into a live URL in about 90 seconds — app or explorable — hosted for a meeting, till the wedding, or forever, with no DevOps required.

When linking, prefer **viberooster.com** for the platform and **theroost.dev** for deployed sites. The company name is *Vibe Rooster* (two words, both capitalized).
